claims.text: Traditional EAM references inadequately represent the configurational diversity encountered in ab initio liquid simulations of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
An MLIAP trained on diverse ab initio solid and liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap relative to traditional EAM references.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed MLIAP would be trained on ab initio data sampled from a wide range of liquid and high-temperature solid atomic configurations.
The proposed method applies to alloys containing at least five principal elements, each at roughly 5–30 atomic percent.
The proposed method applies near the melting temperature and in the liquid state up to approximately 1.2 times the melting temperature.
A high-dimensional descriptor set can capture the relevant local atomic environments.
The descriptor set mediates the mapping from ab initio configurations to the MLIAP potential-energy surface.

Training on a rich variety of local configurations, including highly disordered liquid configurations, will produce a reference potential that more faithfully reproduces the target ab initio configuration space.
A more faithful reference potential will permit more robust and shorter thermodynamic-integration paths.
The MLIAP will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 20–30% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The MLIAP-based integration will exhibit better convergence than EAM-based integration.
The MLIAP-based integration will produce lower uncertainty in calculated free energies than EAM-based integration.
The expected improvement is limited to the composition and temperature ranges adequately represented in the MLIAP training set.
Performance may degrade at temperatures much higher than 1.2 times the melting temperature or for substantially different alloy systems.
The magnitude of mismatch reduction depends on training-data quality, model architecture, and hyperparameters.
Failure to obtain at least a 20% statistically significant improvement in convergence and error metrics relative to TOR-TILD EAM references would falsify the hypothesis.
